rejected.description: Denver is getting a huge, free-to-enter Munich-style Oktoberfest this October. It's running October 16th to 18th and 22nd to 25th at the National Western Center's brand-new Main Campus Plaza, which just opened in January 2026. General admission's completely free, though you'll pay extra for food, beer, and $15 parking. They're also setting up an approximately 110-foot observation wheel, and the scheduled opening ceremony even features a blessing by Lakota elder Doug Good Feather alongside an expected visiting delegation from Germany. So why does a new local festival have this much official international backing? In November 2024, the mayors of Denver and Munich signed an economic partnership to connect both cities. The nonprofit running this event, the Bavarian Guild, built the festival to bring that relationship directly to the public. But this event is only one piece of the partnership. The Colorado Symphony recently started an artistic exchange with a Munich-based orchestra, Munich Airport's academy is adding training modules to a CU Denver graduate program, and organizers plan to bring the festival back in 2027.
